summary: Intermittent artifact fetch TCP RSTs caused by asymmetric return path on VPC peering with TGW route leak
description:
Issue summary: Finovate Labs report intermittent 5xx and presigned-object validation failures during model shard fetches from serving nodes in their private deployment. Impact: downstream model loads fail ~2-5% of requests during high parallelism, causing client-side timeouts and degraded throughput. Environment: private deployment using VPC peering into customer VPC, Transit Gateway present for on-prem connectivity. Observed behavior is correlated with cross-AZ shard fetches and when customer TGW advertises overlapping routes.

Impact: affects production inference for Finovate Labs periodically; manifests as artifact fetch 5xx/403 and long tails in token latency. Customers see model load errors and increased retries.

Template fields:
- Steps to reproduce: see steps_to_reproduce field.
- Relevant logs/metrics: flow logs, tcpdump excerpt, serving node logs included below.
- Current mitigation: temporary static route change applied by Finovate network team to force symmetric return via peering (see resolution_notes).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) From a serving node in Redwood private subnet, request model load that triggers parallel shard fetches (e.g., generate with redwood-open-13b, batch size 8, seq len 1024).
2) Observe intermittent 5xx errors in serving logs for shard GETs to presigned S3 URL (error window ~10-30s).
3) On customer network, run parallel curl requests to the same presigned URL from two AZs across the peering connection and capture tcpdump on the return path.
4) Reproduce reliably under high concurrency and when on-prem TGW is advertising the customer's 10.0.0.0/8 aggregate via propagation to the peering account.
logs: serving-node.log excerpt: GET /presigned-url 200, GET /presigned-url 500 (RST from peer) 2026-03-10T14:23:12Z
tcpdump on customer-egress: src=54.231.12.34:443 dst=10.1.5.12:49152 RST, ack=0 MSS=8960; subsequent SYN retransmit from serving node fails to complete TLS handshake
VPC Flow Log (peered-vpc): Accept START, Accept END, then Reject (RST) coming from IGW ENI at same timestamp 14:23:12Z
control-plane auth logs: token_refresh OK but artifact download failed with HTTP/2 stream reset 103 (peer closed connection)
comments: 2026-03-10 15:02 Maya Chen (Support): Customer reports spikes of shard GET failures correlated with nightly batch ingestion. They can reproduce by firing 200 parallel requests from their batch workers.

2026-03-10 16:15 Liam Rivera (Eng): Collected tcpdump and VPC Flow logs from customer; initial hypothesis: asymmetric routing returning through customer IGW where a firewall/NAT rewrites source causing TCP state mismatch and RSTs.

2026-03-11 09:40 Finovate Labs (Network Ops): Confirmed TGW route propagation was recently changed by their on-prem team; showed routes for 10.0.0.0/8 advertised back to VPC. Applied temporary route suppression to TGW and saw immediate drop in errors.
2026-03-11 11:05 Liam Rivera (Eng): Requested capture of conntrack counters and ephemeral port exhaustion metrics; asked customer to provide firewall logs for RST events around timestamps.
2026-03-12 08:00 Customer Success (CS): Customer applied our temporary fix and reports service returned to normal for last 24h; awaiting permanent changes on their side.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Asymmetric return path due to TGW route propagation caused outbound S3 presigned responses to take a different IGW/ENI with SNAT applied, which changes source IP/port seen by customer firewall -> firewall terminates session with RST because it sees unexpected mapping or short MSS/fragmentation.

Evidence: tcpdump shows RSTs from customer IGW IP with src IP different to original destination (indicates SNAT on return path). VPC Flow Logs show traffic leaving via peering but return via IGW ENI. Timing correlates with TGW route changes made by customer's on-prem team on 2026-03-09.

Control-plane: auth flows remain healthy (tokens refreshed), so issue is at artifact download path (data plane) not control plane auth. Serving runtime retries masks some failures but increases latency and costs.
Test conducted: Customer suppressed route advertisement from TGW and errors dropped to baseline (reproduction rate ~0.1%) -> confirms route asymmetry is root cause.
Additional observation: High parallelism increases chance of ephemeral port reuse and conntrack churn on customer's firewall, amplifying race conditions leading to RSTs.
resolution_notes: Workaround applied (2026-03-11 10:30): Customer removed TGW propagation of overlapping prefix to VPC and added explicit route in VPC route table pointing back to peering attachment to force symmetric routing. This reduced RSTs to near zero.
Temporary firewall recommendation: Increase conntrack table size and widen ephemeral port range to reduce collisions until permanent routing fix is in place.

Permanent fix: Customer to adopt one of the following: 1) adjust TGW route propagation to avoid advertising overlapping aggregates into the peered VPC; or 2) configure TGW route priority and blackhole rules so return path for presigned object IP ranges always traverses the peering attachment; or 3) implement SNAT-free path via VPCE and S3 Gateway endpoints (where applicable).

Redwood action items: add an automated detection rule for asymmetric path evidence (flow logs + tcpdump signature) and create an alert to notify Support when artifact fetch error rate >1% for private deployments.
Customer confirmed full validation 2026-03-12 07:50 and we recommend monitoring 72h before closing ticket.
root_cause: Asymmetric routing caused by TGW route propagation of overlapping prefixes; return packets for presigned S3 object fetches were SNATed by customer IGW/firewall, producing unexpected TCP state that led to RSTs and aborted shard downloads.
mitigation: Suppress TGW route advertisement of overlapping aggregates into the peered VPC to restore symmetric routing.
Temporarily increase firewall conntrack and ephemeral port range on customer perimeter to reduce collisions.
Enable additional retries and longer backoff in serving runtime for artifact fetches while customer routes are corrected (short-term).
follow_up_tasks: Create detection/alert in Redwood Console for asymmetric-return-path signatures (infra ticket https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/1123).
Draft KB article for customers on peering + TGW best practices and recommended route tables for private deployments.
Coordinate with Finovate Labs to schedule a post-change validation and close the ticket after 72h of stable behavior.
